title: Transition order: evidence, contracts in place, relocation, freeze
question: In which order can the redistribution run so that every step has its owner and a safety net?

options.text: Schema first (revision 1): Audit ownership split before its owner and contract exist.
Relocate first: Files move twice and contracts change under moved code.

context: Independent architecture review (revision 2) requested by the owner (brief M6, M7). Phase tasks and implementation remain deferred. Revision 1 split installers and audit ownership in P1 before the participant contract and the Audit module existed.
decision: P1 captures 0.7.0 evidence and builds the compatibility harness and boundary scans in report mode without production changes; P2 performs the single API/SPI transition in place, making existing scope, audit and generator code use the final contracts; P3 relocates complete module slices and splits schema, installer, health and config ownership; P4 qualifies one candidate and freezes baselines. Each phase leaves main releasable as 0.x.
rationale: Moving installation, insertion and pruning together needs the participant contract and the Audit module; contracts first means files move only once; evidence first makes every later change measurable against 0.7.0.
consequences: P1 changes only tests and CI.
Responsibilities move between phases only by explicit plan amendment.

evidence.note: Owner requested an independent review and authorized amending Codex decisions within the owner principles.
